question: #283 gate: per backend, is the ptracer out of the syscall hot path?
method: marginal wall per guest syscall = (T(50000)-T(2000))/48000, median of 3, fixture = N getppid() calls; coverage control via DETLOG inbound-syscall counts; TracerPid read by the guest from /proc/self/status

key_findings.only_passing_backend: dbi (1.43 us/syscall vs ptrace 34.13, at equal 200/200 coverage)
key_findings.tracerpid_does_not_discriminate: all backends including dbi show TracerPid=1; attachment != per-syscall round-trip
key_findings.e9patch_matches_ptrace: 34.31 vs 34.13 us, consistent with its documented 'then use the ptrace runtime'
key_findings.kvm: UNMEASURABLE - killed at 400s timeout on a trivial guest; contradicts the task's 'KVM may already qualify' prior
key_findings.liteinst: BLOCKED - preload handshake failure, root-caused separately

measurement_artifact_avoided: --log-file under /tmp yields zero records because hermit isolates guest /tmp; an earlier pass read that as 'e9patch intercepts nothing'
